requirements.text: The kernel MUST NOT evaluate an ACR guard while handling a system call, an interrupt, a memory fault, a context switch or the completion of an input or output operation.
requirements.evidence: system calls, the timer interrupt, faults from user mode and the switch between processes exist and evaluate no guard (`user.rs` calls none; the kernel records processes in its register after they have all ended). No input or output completion path exists

requirements.text: An ACR guard MUST be evaluated only when an event is offered to a register.
requirements.evidence: the guards are reachable only through `Record::submit`, `Record::open` and `Record::extend` in the core

requirements.text: For a writer that has already checked a register, the cost of offering one more event MUST NOT grow with the number of events already in it, beyond reading the file.
requirements.evidence: measured in this build at 0.28 ms per stored event at 100, 500 and 2,000 events, each event written durably; before this build it was 1.25 ms, 5.3 ms and 21 ms. Test: continuing a checked record equals checking the whole, at every split

requirements.text: While ACR is not in use, the system MUST do no ACR work beyond establishing that it is not in use.
requirements.evidence: for the host program: a hook with no register present reads nothing and writes nothing. DESIGN for the kernel

requirements.text: The kernel MUST NOT schedule, delay or reprioritise a task because of the state of a review.
requirements.evidence: the scheduler takes the next process in turn and reads nothing else; the kernel holds no review, so the rule has not been tested against one

requirements.text: A halt of ACR use MUST be accepted in every state in which anything is in use.
requirements.evidence: state-machine test over every state; host tests for a mismatched label, a register holding a refused event, and 64 open reviews

requirements.text: The system MUST start and be usable on a machine with no graphics processor, no network and no accelerator.
requirements.evidence: today it has no use for any of them

requirements.text: The system MUST NOT open a network connection that the person directing it did not cause.
requirements.evidence: the LINK state machine starts OFFLINE and the guards refuse a retrieved artifact without its source; there is no network stack to enforce it on

requirements.text: The kernel MUST contain no code from another kernel and MUST NOT require another operating system to start.
requirements.evidence: its only dependency is the PCP OS core; it is started directly by a Multiboot loader

requirements.text: Before enabling a processor feature, the kernel MUST ask the processor whether it offers that feature, and MUST report and stop where a required one is absent.
requirements.evidence: started as two processors without long mode; each printed the reason and halted

requirements.text: No memory MUST be both writable and executable.
requirements.evidence: the page tables are read back and the count is zero; a write to code, a write to read-only data and execution of data are each attempted and refused by the processor

requirements.text: The kernel MUST map its own image and nothing else.
requirements.evidence: 2,209 pages from 1 MiB to the end of the image; reads of the display memory, the low mebibyte and memory above the image are attempted and refused. Before this build the whole first gibibyte was mapped writable

requirements.text: The interrupt table, the segment table and the task state segment MUST be read-only once set.
requirements.evidence: a write to each is attempted and refused

requirements.text: A double fault, a non-maskable interrupt and a machine check MUST each be delivered on a stack of their own, and every stack MUST have an unmapped page below it.
requirements.evidence: a read of each of the five guard pages is refused (the kernel stack, the three fault stacks and the stack for entries from user mode); the stack-exhaustion demonstration ends in a reported double fault

requirements.text: The kernel MUST turn on supervisor execution prevention, supervisor access prevention and user-mode instruction prevention wherever the processor offers them.
requirements.evidence: read back from the control register on a processor with all three and on one with none

requirements.text: An exception the kernel did not prepare for MUST stop the kernel with a report, and MUST NOT be continued past.
requirements.evidence: the fault demonstration

requirements.text: Arithmetic overflow in the kernel MUST stop the kernel.
requirements.evidence: overflow checks are compiled into the release build

requirements.text: Code that the compiler cannot check for memory safety MUST be confined to one named module, and each use MUST state why it is sound.
requirements.evidence: `arch.rs` only; every other file refuses it at compile time

requirements.text: The kernel MUST record its own start, verification and stop in a register, and verification MUST end in OPERATIONAL or in SAFE and nothing else.
requirements.evidence: the kernel's register replays with no problem

requirements.text: The kernel MUST measure its running image and compare the measurement with a value it did not compute.
requirements.evidence: it measures. There is nothing yet to compare with: no signed image and no measured start

requirements.text: No code supplied by a third party MUST run in kernel mode.
The kernel SHOULD be loaded at an address that differs between starts.
requirements.evidence: it is loaded at a fixed address

requirements.text: The kernel MUST have a source of randomness before it issues any identifier or key.
Authority MUST be held as capabilities, and a capability derived from another MUST carry the same rights or fewer.
requirements.evidence: in the core: derivation, narrowing and revocation tests. PARTIAL in the kernel: each process is a holder, and the write call is answered only for a process that holds a capability for the console (self-test: a program started without it is refused). One object and one right; no capability passes between processes

requirements.text: There MUST be no identity that holds every right.
No combination of roles MUST give a model or a program the right to start ACR use, to administer, or to change the system.
requirements.evidence: exhaustive over every kind of identity, set of roles and edition

requirements.text: Administration MUST be a role held by a person and exercised only while the system is in MAINTENANCE.
requirements.evidence: the SYSTEM state machine has MAINTENANCE and its transitions, and entering it asks every task to stop. Nothing yet enforces it on a running system

requirements.text: Every administrative act MUST be an event in the register before it takes effect.
In the Commercial and Enterprise Editions, whoever administers an installation MUST NOT assess under it.
requirements.evidence: stated in the edition profile; the host program refuses a two-person standard in the Personal Edition; separation of the two roles is not enforced

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: Every register MUST state the method release it is held to, by digest.

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A review MUST keep the method release and the modules it was commissioned under until it is closed.
requirements.evidence: for modules, which are fixed in the commission event. PARTIAL for the release, which is fixed per register

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: Adding or removing a module MUST require no change to any program.
requirements.evidence: in the host program, the plugins and the machine form: a module is found by the header of its own Specification, and a test adds one the program has never heard of. The method packet's own Python tools still carry a list

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A commission MUST name each selected module by identifier, version and the digest of its Specification, and each MUST be a module found in the method text at hand.
requirements.evidence: tests for a wrong digest, a wrong version, an unknown module, Core listed, and a module listed twice

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A module written for another Core than the one a program implements MUST NOT be selected.

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A participant MUST NOT select a module; selection is the act of the person directing the work or of a policy they set.
requirements.evidence: recorded by the host from a typed command or a terminal; refused from a session

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A licensee MAY modify a module or add their own.
requirements.evidence: adding is a supported path in the host program (`pcpos module add`): the module stands beside the register, the addition is recorded with the digest of its Specification, and a review selects it by that digest. Modifying a released module is not a supported path: a changed file is found, its real digest is used, and the register records that the method text at hand differs from the release

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: A module that is not a released module MUST NOT carry the identifier of one.
requirements.evidence: the host program accepts an added module only under an identifier beginning `local.`, refuses one that takes the name of a module of the method, and serves no text for an identifier that two folders claim. A folder placed by hand inside the method text itself and named `acr.<new name>` is still listed as a module; the register's method check then reports the text as differing from the release

section.title: What of ACR can be changed, when, and by whom

requirements.text: The person who owns the machine MAY replace any program outside the kernel image and MAY rebuild the image.
A record MUST state what produced each observation it holds: which participant, and whether the host observed it or a participant reported it.
requirements.evidence: actor, authority, `read_by`, `observed` and the task worker are recorded. Since build 18 a check says how the record came by it: `HOST_OBSERVED_TOOL` where the host saw the shell command run and passed on its exit status and output, `REPORTED_BY_PARTICIPANT` where a participant gave its own account, which is all that builds before 18 could record. The host's observation is of the command and its output as the host reported them; it is not an observation that the command tests anything. Since build 19 the observation must have been made after the open review was commissioned, a finding that rests only on reported checks is marked `execution: UNKNOWN`, and material that reaches the record while a review is open is recorded by how it came (words the host did not see the person type, and a file written since commissioning, as PRODUCED). The observations are kept in an ordinary file that a shell command can write: none of this is authentication

requirements.text: System services MUST NOT hold a capability to an interpreter or a compiler.
requirements.evidence: the host program depends on no interpreter and runs none, clause lookup included. Capabilities between services do not exist yet

requirements.text: Where two implementations of the core disagree, the Rust implementation MUST govern.
requirements.evidence: the Python implementation is run against 17,113 cases published by the Rust one

requirements.text: A finding MUST NOT be recorded as supported or as refuted where all that it cites is text the review itself produced.
requirements.evidence: both implementations refuse it (Core 4.3, 5.2), for an artifact recorded as produced after the review was commissioned and for what a task of the review returned. What the guards cannot do is tell a claim that a procedure settles from one that reading settles: the participant declares the kind of claim, and the status shows for each finding whether a check was run and who saw it

requirements.text: Code in C or C++ MUST run in T2.
The core MUST have one stable binary interface, in the C calling convention, and every binding for another language MUST be a thin layer over it that adds no rule.
requirements.evidence: today the core is reached as a Rust library, through the tool server and at a terminal. The Python implementation is a second implementation, not a binding, and is to become one

requirements.text: Every way of reaching a register MUST go through the same core and the same guards.
requirements.evidence: the terminal commands, the tool server and the hooks are one program over one core

requirements.text: A caller MUST NOT be able to name the actor of an event.
The interface for models MUST be the Model Context Protocol.
requirements.evidence: revisions 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25; tools only

requirements.text: Material retrieved from outside MUST be recorded with where and when it was retrieved.
requirements.evidence: in the guards

requirements.text: An extension MUST be a package with a manifest stating its identity, its digest, its tier and the capabilities it asks for.
requirements.evidence: The two PCP plugins for Claude are packages of this shape for another host

requirements.text: An extension MUST NOT run in kernel mode.
An extension MUST receive only the capabilities the person granted it, and installing, granting and revoking MUST each be recorded.
Revoking a capability MUST take back everything derived from it, in every holder.
requirements.evidence: in the core

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: The system MUST use the display at its native resolution as the firmware reports it, and SHOULD choose the default scale from the display's physical density.
requirements.evidence: the kernel has no display code

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: Default backgrounds MUST be drawn at the display's own resolution from a resolution-independent description, and MUST use the design tokens of the edition and the workspace.
requirements.evidence: the backgrounds exist as vector files generated from the tokens. Nothing displays them

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: Every record MUST carry time in UTC.

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: The time zone MUST be a setting of each person, used for display only, and setting it MUST NOT need a network.

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: First start MUST create the person who directs the system before anything else is allowed, and MUST NOT require an account with any service.

section.title: Devices, display, time and first start

requirements.text: A graphics processor MUST be a device like any other: used by whoever holds a capability to it, absent without consequence.
